# Conservative Party Manifesto 2015: Summary

## Economic Foundation
The manifesto centers on continuing the Conservative "long-term economic plan" following five years of deficit reduction. The party pledges to eliminate the deficit entirely and achieve a budget surplus by 2018-19, claiming Britain had become the fastest-growing major advanced economy. Key fiscal commitments include no increases to VAT, Income Tax, or National Insurance, while raising the tax-free Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the 40p threshold to £50,000.

## Life Stage Promises

**For Families and Children:** The manifesto promises 30 hours of free childcare for working parents of 3-4 year olds, 200,000 new Starter Homes at 20% below market price for first-time buyers under 40, and extending Right to Buy to Housing Association tenants.

**For Workers:** Commitments include creating 3 million apprenticeships, taking minimum wage earners out of Income Tax entirely, and pursuing "full employment" by creating 2 million new jobs. The party pledges to crack down on tax evasion while supporting small businesses through reduced red tape.

**For Pensioners:** The triple lock on state pensions continues (rising by at least 2.5%, inflation, or earnings—whichever highest). The effective Inheritance Tax threshold for couples would rise to £1 million, and pension freedoms would be maintained.

## Public Services

**NHS:** An additional £8 billion above inflation by 2020, implementing a truly 7-day NHS with same-day GP appointments guaranteed for over-75s. Mental health receives equal priority with physical health.

**Education:** Every failing secondary school to become an academy, 500 new free schools, and maintaining per-pupil funding levels.

## Immigration and EU
The party commits to reducing net migration to "tens of thousands," reforming EU welfare rules so migrants must work four years before claiming benefits, and holding an in-out EU referendum by end of 2017. The Human Rights Act would be scrapped and replaced with a British Bill of Rights.

## Infrastructure and Devolution
Major investments include £13 billion for Northern transport (the "Northern Powerhouse"), High Speed 2 and 3 rail links, and universal superfast broadband by 2017. English votes for English laws would be implemented, alongside honoring the Smith Commission for Scottish devolution.

## Security
Defence spending meets NATO's 2% target, maintaining Trident nuclear deterrent, and keeping regular armed forces at current levels. Counter-terrorism powers would be strengthened with new Extremism Disruption Orders.

## International Commitments
The 0.7% GDP aid commitment continues, with goals to save 1.4 million children's lives through immunization and help 11 million children access education by 2020.
